From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/LRB_Aria.jpg/250px-LRB_Aria.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LRB_Aria.jpg)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/LittleRiverBandOct06.jpg/250px-LittleRiverBandOct06.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LittleRiverBandOct06.jpg)

Members of Little River Band in 2004 (top) and 2006 (bottom)

Little River Band (LRB) were formed in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne"), [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(Australia) "Victoria (Australia)"), Australia, in March 1975. The original Australian group featured lead vocalist [Glenn Shorrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Shorrock "Glenn Shorrock"), guitarists and vocalists [Beeb Birtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeb_Birtles "Beeb Birtles") and [Graeham Goble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graeham_Goble "Graeham Goble"), lead guitarist [Ric Formosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ric_Formosa "Ric Formosa"), bassist [Roger McLachlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_McLachlan "Roger McLachlan") and drummer [Derek Pellicci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Pellicci "Derek Pellicci"). Since their formation, the band have been through numerous lineup changes. None of the original Australian band are members of the current American band which have legal use of the Little River Band name and trademarks. This band includes bassist and lead vocalist [Wayne Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Nelson "Wayne Nelson") (from 1980 to 1996 and since 1999), keyboardist and vocalist [Chris Marion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Marion "Chris Marion") (since 2004), drummer and vocalist Ryan Ricks (since 2012), guitarist and vocalist Colin Whinnery (since 2018) and guitarist and vocalist Bruce Wallace (since 2022).

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### 1975–82

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1975–82")]

LRB were formed in March 1975 by lead vocalist Glenn Shorrock, guitarist-vocalists Beeb Birtles and Graeham Goble, lead guitarist Ric Formosa, bassist Roger McLachlan and drummer Derek Pellicci.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2) The previous month, before taking on its new name, the group had recorded a [cover version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") of the [Everly Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Everly_Brothers "The Everly Brothers") song "[When Will I Be Loved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When_Will_I_Be_Loved_(song) "When Will I Be Loved (song)")" with lead guitarist [Graham Davidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Davidge "Graham Davidge") and bassist [Dave Orams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Orams "Dave Orams"), however this remained unreleased until 1988 when it was featured on the compilation _[Too Late to Load](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too\_Late\_to\_Load "Too Late to Load")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-3) With the original lineup, LRB recorded its [self-titled 1975 debut album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_River_Band_(album) "Little River Band (album)") and follow-up _[After Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After\_Hours\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "After Hours (Little River Band album)")_, before Formosa left in August 1976; he was replaced by [David Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Briggs_(Australian_musician) "David Briggs (Australian musician)"), while the group also brought in George McArdle to take over from McLachlan, with whom they "weren't 100 per cent happy".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-4)

With Briggs and McArdle, LRB achieved international success with the releases of _[Diamantina Cocktail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamantina\_Cocktail "Diamantina Cocktail")_ in 1977 and _[Sleeper Catcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper\_Catcher "Sleeper Catcher")_ in 1978.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2) For a world tour in the summer of 1978, Pellicci was temporarily replaced by [Geoff Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Cox "Geoff Cox"), a former bandmate of Briggs in the band Cycle, after suffering burn injuries which rendered him unable to perform.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-cox-5) At the same time, Mal Logan was brought in as a touring keyboardist.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-logan-6) Following Pellicci's return, the group recorded three shows in November 1978 for its first live album, _[Backstage Pass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstage\_Pass\_(album) "Backstage Pass (album)")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) At the end of January 1979, however, McArdle also left after [converting to Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_again "Born again") and deciding to attend [Bible college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible_college "Bible college") full-time.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-8) He was not immediately replaced, with bass on _[First Under the Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First\_Under\_the\_Wire "First Under the Wire")_ performed by session musicians Clive Harrison and Mike Clarke.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-9)

In July 1979, McArdle's official replacement was announced to be Barry Sullivan.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-10) He remained for less than a year, however, before former [Jim Messina Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Messina_(musician) "Jim Messina (musician)") bassist [Wayne Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Nelson "Wayne Nelson") took over in April 1980.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-11) The new lineup recorded _[Time Exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_Exposure\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Time Exposure (Little River Band album)")_ in 1981, although before it was released Briggs left the group.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-12) He was replaced in August 1981 by [Stephen Housden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Housden "Stephen Housden"), formerly of [Stevie Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wright "Stevie Wright")'s band.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-13) Following a world tour which spawned the live video _[Live Exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_Exposure "Live Exposure")_, frontman Shorrock left LRB in February 1982 to focus on his solo career.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-14) In subsequent years, Shorrock has claimed that he did not leave the band voluntarily, and was instead sacked.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-15) Nelson has supported the claim, suggesting that guitarist Beeb Birtles "voted to oust" the singer which led to the band subsequently "dismantling".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-nelson-16)

### 1982–98

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1982–98")]

Glenn Shorrock was replaced in February 1982 by [John Farnham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Farnham "John Farnham").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-17) His first recording with LRB was "[The Other Guy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Other_Guy_(song) "The Other Guy (song)")", which was released on the compilation _[Greatest Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest\_Hits\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Greatest Hits (Little River Band album)")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-18) Following the release of _[The Net](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Net\_(album) "The Net (album)")_, the band added its first official keyboardist in [David Hirschfelder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hirschfelder "David Hirschfelder"), who joined in time for tour dates in September 1983.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) Within six months of his arrival, the group had lost two more founding members – [Beeb Birtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeb_Birtles "Beeb Birtles") left in October 1983 and [Derek Pellicci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Pellicci "Derek Pellicci") followed in February 1984, both due to stylistic differences.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-19) Birtles was not replaced, while former [Cold Chisel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Chisel "Cold Chisel") drummer [Steve Prestwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Prestwich "Steve Prestwich") took over from Pellicci ready for the recording of _[Playing to Win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playing\_to\_Win\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Playing to Win (Little River Band album)")_ in July 1984.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-20) A second album, _[No Reins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No\_Reins "No Reins")_, followed in 1986.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-21)

For a short Australian tour in April 1986, Prestwich was replaced by touring drummer Malcolm Wakeford.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) However, this would prove to be the final tour with several band members, and the band's last activity for almost two years, as Farnham left in October that year to focus on his solo career.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-22) The group subsequently disbanded, citing "frustration over diminishing record sales and radio airplay".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-23) After months of rumours, LRB officially reformed in December 1987 with original lead singer [Glenn Shorrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Shorrock "Glenn Shorrock").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-24) Stephen Housden, Graeham Goble and Wayne Nelson returned from the 1986 lineup, alongside original drummer Derek Pellicci.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-25) James Roche joined as the band's touring keyboardist.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) This lineup issued _[Monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Monsoon (Little River Band album)")_ in 1988 and _[Get Lucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get\_Lucky\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Get Lucky (Little River Band album)")_ in 1990.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/GG7591_Cover.jpg/250px-GG7591_Cover.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GG7591_Cover.jpg)

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GG7591_Cover.jpg "File:GG7591 Cover.jpg")

[Graeham Goble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graeham_Goble "Graeham Goble") became the last constant member to leave LRB when he ceased touring in April 1989, before leaving permanently in 1992. 

Goble – now the sole constant member of LRB – performed his last shows with the band in April 1989.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) It was officially announced in March the next year that he would no longer tour with the group, in order to focus primarily on his side project Broken Voices.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-26) He was replaced by former [Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_(band) "Player (band)") frontman [Peter Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Beckett "Peter Beckett"), while [Tony Sciuto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Sciuto "Tony Sciuto") joined as the group's new keyboardist.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-27) This lineup issued _[Worldwide Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide\_Love "Worldwide Love")_ in 1991, a compilation on which the title track was a new recording.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-beckett-28) By summer 1992, Goble had left permanently and Sciuto had been temporarily replaced by Richard Bryant.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-29) After a tour which spawned the live album _[Live Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_Classics "Live Classics")_, Sciuto returned.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-beckett-28)

In 1996, both lead vocalists Shorrock and Nelson left LRB, replaced by [Steve Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Wade_(singer) "Steve Wade (singer)") and Hal Tupaea, respectively.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-30) After a touring cycle which ran until late 1997, Beckett left the band to return to Player, to which he also brought Sciuto.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-beckett-28) Pellicci also left for a second time, leaving the group with no founding members for the first time in its history.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-31) At this point, Stephen Housden acquired the rights to the LRB band name, after Shorrock reportedly declined an offer to rejoin the outfit.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-nelson-16)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-32)

### Since 1998

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Since 1998")]

Retaining Steve Wade as frontman, Stephen Housden rebuilt LRB in early 1998 with the addition of [Icehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Icehouse_(band) "Icehouse (band)") guitarist [Paul Gildea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Gildea "Paul Gildea"), original LRB bassist [Roger McLachlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_McLachlan "Roger McLachlan"), drummer Kevin Murphy and former Air Supply keyboardist Adrian Scott.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-33) McLachlan and Scott remained only for a year, before they were replaced in early 1999 by returning [Wayne Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Nelson "Wayne Nelson") and new member Glenn Reither.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-34) One year later, Gildea was replaced by Greg Hind.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-35) Wade also left the group at the same time, at which point Nelson took over as the band's lead vocalist.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-36) This lineup issued the group's first studio album in 11 years, _Where We Started From_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2)

Shortly after the release of _Test of Time_ in 2004, Reither was replaced by [Chris Marion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Marion "Chris Marion").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-37) Murphy was also briefly replaced by Kip Raines, although he was unable to commit to the band full-time and was himself replaced early the next year by Billy Thomas.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-38) In March 2006, LRB's longest-running continuous member Stephen Housden stepped down from touring, with Rich Herring brought in to take his place.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-39) This lineup released studio album _Re-arranged_ and live collection _Standing Room Only_, before Thomas was replaced by Mel Watts in early 2007.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-40) Watts remained until early 2012, recording two [Christmas albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_music "Christmas music") with the group, before he was replaced by Ryan Ricks.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-41) During 2017, Hind was briefly unable to tour due to a [carpal tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpal_tunnel_syndrome "Carpal tunnel syndrome") injury, with Colin Whinnery temporarily taking his place; Whinnery returned on a permanent basis early the next year, after Hind chose to leave following a series of family issues.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-42) In 2022, Bruce Wallace replaced Rich Herring on guitar and vocals.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-43)

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/af/LRB_Aria.jpg/250px-LRB_Aria.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LRB_Aria.jpg)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/LittleRiverBandOct06.jpg/250px-LittleRiverBandOct06.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LittleRiverBandOct06.jpg)

Members of Little River Band in 2004 (top) and 2006 (bottom)

Little River Band (LRB) were formed in [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne"), [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_(Australia) "Victoria (Australia)"), Australia, in March 1975. The original Australian group featured lead vocalist [Glenn Shorrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Shorrock "Glenn Shorrock"), guitarists and vocalists [Beeb Birtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeb_Birtles "Beeb Birtles") and [Graeham Goble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graeham_Goble "Graeham Goble"), lead guitarist [Ric Formosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ric_Formosa "Ric Formosa"), bassist [Roger McLachlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_McLachlan "Roger McLachlan") and drummer [Derek Pellicci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Pellicci "Derek Pellicci"). Since their formation, the band have been through numerous lineup changes. None of the original Australian band are members of the current American band which have legal use of the Little River Band name and trademarks. This band includes bassist and lead vocalist [Wayne Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Nelson "Wayne Nelson") (from 1980 to 1996 and since 1999), keyboardist and vocalist [Chris Marion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Marion "Chris Marion") (since 2004), drummer and vocalist Ryan Ricks (since 2012), guitarist and vocalist Colin Whinnery (since 2018) and guitarist and vocalist Bruce Wallace (since 2022).

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### 1975–82

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1975–82")]

LRB were formed in March 1975 by lead vocalist Glenn Shorrock, guitarist-vocalists Beeb Birtles and Graeham Goble, lead guitarist Ric Formosa, bassist Roger McLachlan and drummer Derek Pellicci.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2) The previous month, before taking on its new name, the group had recorded a [cover version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version") of the [Everly Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Everly_Brothers "The Everly Brothers") song "[When Will I Be Loved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/When_Will_I_Be_Loved_(song) "When Will I Be Loved (song)")" with lead guitarist [Graham Davidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Davidge "Graham Davidge") and bassist [Dave Orams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Orams "Dave Orams"), however this remained unreleased until 1988 when it was featured on the compilation _[Too Late to Load](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Too\_Late\_to\_Load "Too Late to Load")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-3) With the original lineup, LRB recorded its [self-titled 1975 debut album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_River_Band_(album) "Little River Band (album)") and follow-up _[After Hours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/After\_Hours\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "After Hours (Little River Band album)")_, before Formosa left in August 1976; he was replaced by [David Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Briggs_(Australian_musician) "David Briggs (Australian musician)"), while the group also brought in George McArdle to take over from McLachlan, with whom they "weren't 100 per cent happy".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-4)

With Briggs and McArdle, LRB achieved international success with the releases of _[Diamantina Cocktail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamantina\_Cocktail "Diamantina Cocktail")_ in 1977 and _[Sleeper Catcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper\_Catcher "Sleeper Catcher")_ in 1978.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2) For a world tour in the summer of 1978, Pellicci was temporarily replaced by [Geoff Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Cox "Geoff Cox"), a former bandmate of Briggs in the band Cycle, after suffering burn injuries which rendered him unable to perform.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-cox-5) At the same time, Mal Logan was brought in as a touring keyboardist.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-logan-6) Following Pellicci's return, the group recorded three shows in November 1978 for its first live album, _[Backstage Pass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backstage\_Pass\_(album) "Backstage Pass (album)")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) At the end of January 1979, however, McArdle also left after [converting to Christianity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Born_again "Born again") and deciding to attend [Bible college](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bible_college "Bible college") full-time.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-8) He was not immediately replaced, with bass on _[First Under the Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First\_Under\_the\_Wire "First Under the Wire")_ performed by session musicians Clive Harrison and Mike Clarke.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-9)

In July 1979, McArdle's official replacement was announced to be Barry Sullivan.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-10) He remained for less than a year, however, before former [Jim Messina Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Messina_(musician) "Jim Messina (musician)") bassist [Wayne Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Nelson "Wayne Nelson") took over in April 1980.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-11) The new lineup recorded _[Time Exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_Exposure\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Time Exposure (Little River Band album)")_ in 1981, although before it was released Briggs left the group.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-12) He was replaced in August 1981 by [Stephen Housden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Housden "Stephen Housden"), formerly of [Stevie Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Wright "Stevie Wright")'s band.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-13) Following a world tour which spawned the live video _[Live Exposure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_Exposure "Live Exposure")_, frontman Shorrock left LRB in February 1982 to focus on his solo career.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-14) In subsequent years, Shorrock has claimed that he did not leave the band voluntarily, and was instead sacked.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-15) Nelson has supported the claim, suggesting that guitarist Beeb Birtles "voted to oust" the singer which led to the band subsequently "dismantling".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-nelson-16)

### 1982–98

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1982–98")]

Glenn Shorrock was replaced in February 1982 by [John Farnham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Farnham "John Farnham").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-17) His first recording with LRB was "[The Other Guy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Other_Guy_(song) "The Other Guy (song)")", which was released on the compilation _[Greatest Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greatest\_Hits\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Greatest Hits (Little River Band album)")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-18) Following the release of _[The Net](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Net\_(album) "The Net (album)")_, the band added its first official keyboardist in [David Hirschfelder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Hirschfelder "David Hirschfelder"), who joined in time for tour dates in September 1983.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) Within six months of his arrival, the group had lost two more founding members – [Beeb Birtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeb_Birtles "Beeb Birtles") left in October 1983 and [Derek Pellicci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derek_Pellicci "Derek Pellicci") followed in February 1984, both due to stylistic differences.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-19) Birtles was not replaced, while former [Cold Chisel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_Chisel "Cold Chisel") drummer [Steve Prestwich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Prestwich "Steve Prestwich") took over from Pellicci ready for the recording of _[Playing to Win](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playing\_to\_Win\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Playing to Win (Little River Band album)")_ in July 1984.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-20) A second album, _[No Reins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No\_Reins "No Reins")_, followed in 1986.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-21)

For a short Australian tour in April 1986, Prestwich was replaced by touring drummer Malcolm Wakeford.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) However, this would prove to be the final tour with several band members, and the band's last activity for almost two years, as Farnham left in October that year to focus on his solo career.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-22) The group subsequently disbanded, citing "frustration over diminishing record sales and radio airplay".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-23) After months of rumours, LRB officially reformed in December 1987 with original lead singer [Glenn Shorrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Shorrock "Glenn Shorrock").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-24) Stephen Housden, Graeham Goble and Wayne Nelson returned from the 1986 lineup, alongside original drummer Derek Pellicci.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-25) James Roche joined as the band's touring keyboardist.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) This lineup issued _[Monsoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsoon\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Monsoon (Little River Band album)")_ in 1988 and _[Get Lucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Get\_Lucky\_(Little\_River\_Band\_album) "Get Lucky (Little River Band album)")_ in 1990.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d4/GG7591_Cover.jpg/250px-GG7591_Cover.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GG7591_Cover.jpg)

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:GG7591_Cover.jpg "File:GG7591 Cover.jpg")

[Graeham Goble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graeham_Goble "Graeham Goble") became the last constant member to leave LRB when he ceased touring in April 1989, before leaving permanently in 1992. 

Goble – now the sole constant member of LRB – performed his last shows with the band in April 1989.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-shows-7) It was officially announced in March the next year that he would no longer tour with the group, in order to focus primarily on his side project Broken Voices.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-26) He was replaced by former [Player](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_(band) "Player (band)") frontman [Peter Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Beckett "Peter Beckett"), while [Tony Sciuto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Sciuto "Tony Sciuto") joined as the group's new keyboardist.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-27) This lineup issued _[Worldwide Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worldwide\_Love "Worldwide Love")_ in 1991, a compilation on which the title track was a new recording.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-beckett-28) By summer 1992, Goble had left permanently and Sciuto had been temporarily replaced by Richard Bryant.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-29) After a tour which spawned the live album _[Live Classics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live\_Classics "Live Classics")_, Sciuto returned.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-beckett-28)

In 1996, both lead vocalists Shorrock and Nelson left LRB, replaced by [Steve Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Wade_(singer) "Steve Wade (singer)") and Hal Tupaea, respectively.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-30) After a touring cycle which ran until late 1997, Beckett left the band to return to Player, to which he also brought Sciuto.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-beckett-28) Pellicci also left for a second time, leaving the group with no founding members for the first time in its history.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-31) At this point, Stephen Housden acquired the rights to the LRB band name, after Shorrock reportedly declined an offer to rejoin the outfit.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-nelson-16)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-32)

### Since 1998

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Little_River_Band_members&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Since 1998")]

Retaining Steve Wade as frontman, Stephen Housden rebuilt LRB in early 1998 with the addition of [Icehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Icehouse_(band) "Icehouse (band)") guitarist [Paul Gildea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Gildea "Paul Gildea"), original LRB bassist [Roger McLachlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_McLachlan "Roger McLachlan"), drummer Kevin Murphy and former Air Supply keyboardist Adrian Scott.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-33) McLachlan and Scott remained only for a year, before they were replaced in early 1999 by returning [Wayne Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Nelson "Wayne Nelson") and new member Glenn Reither.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-34) One year later, Gildea was replaced by Greg Hind.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-35) Wade also left the group at the same time, at which point Nelson took over as the band's lead vocalist.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-36) This lineup issued the group's first studio album in 11 years, _Where We Started From_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-allmusic-2)

Shortly after the release of _Test of Time_ in 2004, Reither was replaced by [Chris Marion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Marion "Chris Marion").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-37) Murphy was also briefly replaced by Kip Raines, although he was unable to commit to the band full-time and was himself replaced early the next year by Billy Thomas.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-38) In March 2006, LRB's longest-running continuous member Stephen Housden stepped down from touring, with Rich Herring brought in to take his place.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-39) This lineup released studio album _Re-arranged_ and live collection _Standing Room Only_, before Thomas was replaced by Mel Watts in early 2007.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-40) Watts remained until early 2012, recording two [Christmas albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_music "Christmas music") with the group, before he was replaced by Ryan Ricks.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-41) During 2017, Hind was briefly unable to tour due to a [carpal tunnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpal_tunnel_syndrome "Carpal tunnel syndrome") injury, with Colin Whinnery temporarily taking his place; Whinnery returned on a permanent basis early the next year, after Hind chose to leave following a series of family issues.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-42) In 2022, Bruce Wallace replaced Rich Herring on guitar and vocals.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Little_River_Band_members#cite_note-43)

# NEWSLETTER – FEBRUARY 2025

by [littleriverband](https://reallittleriverband.com/author/littleriverband/ "Posts by littleriverband") | Feb 14, 2025 | [Blog](https://reallittleriverband.com/category/blog/) | [25 comments](https://reallittleriverband.com/2025/02/14/newsletter-february-2025/#respond)

![Image 20](https://reallittleriverband.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/lrblogofeatured.jpg)

Hey Everybody

Little River Band is 50 years old this year!! The Happy Anniversary Tour has kicked off with a bang. We’ll go coast to coast and corner to corner of the US again this year. We’ll park the bus and truck in at least 35 states during 2025, appearing with lots of old friends…Orleans, John Waite, Ambrosia, and Three Dog Night to name(drop) a few. And the booking year is just beginning…who knows what else is in store for our calendar!

Canada…we certainly haven’t forgotten about you either. Windsor ON is on the books for May. We’re hoping for more CA shows to be added so we can get up North for a while. Your support for Little River Band is rivaled only by that in the US. We’re hoping to see you again too!

We’ve changed up the set list a bit…added a couple songs from “the vault”, and thrown in a new and unique feature for LRB. We’ll leave it as a surprise for now, but it’s being mentioned in reviews and is a crowd pleaser.

You may have caught that there’s a truck in the entourage now. We’re carrying our own lights to make the show look and feel more dynamic. Our trailer was maxed out…full to overflowing. So we cut it loose and now put all the gear in a semi. It’s an easier and safer way to travel for the gear and for the crew. Lifting and stacking was taking a toll on everyone. Now we can get in and out of a venue more quickly with all cases on wheels.

We also spent a lot of time and effort in 2024 to clean up our social media accounts and give our website a facelift. If you check out any of those platforms, you’ll see we’re having a good time documenting our down time before and after a show. There’s a lot of joy in the air.

It’s an honor to have your valued support, and to be a part of Little River Band’s long history of great music and great shows. And it’s a lot of fun to let you see what we’re up to before the lights go down at showtime.

Thanks for staying in touch and keeping up with the tour. We’ll see you out there somewhere…

Take Care  
 LRB and Crew

# NEWSLETTER – FEBRUARY 2025

by [littleriverband](https://reallittleriverband.com/author/littleriverband/ "Posts by littleriverband") | Feb 14, 2025 | [Blog](https://reallittleriverband.com/category/blog/) | [25 comments](https://reallittleriverband.com/2025/02/14/newsletter-february-2025/#respond)

![Image 20](https://reallittleriverband.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/lrblogofeatured.jpg)

Hey Everybody

Little River Band is 50 years old this year!! The Happy Anniversary Tour has kicked off with a bang. We’ll go coast to coast and corner to corner of the US again this year. We’ll park the bus and truck in at least 35 states during 2025, appearing with lots of old friends…Orleans, John Waite, Ambrosia, and Three Dog Night to name(drop) a few. And the booking year is just beginning…who knows what else is in store for our calendar!

Canada…we certainly haven’t forgotten about you either. Windsor ON is on the books for May. We’re hoping for more CA shows to be added so we can get up North for a while. Your support for Little River Band is rivaled only by that in the US. We’re hoping to see you again too!

We’ve changed up the set list a bit…added a couple songs from “the vault”, and thrown in a new and unique feature for LRB. We’ll leave it as a surprise for now, but it’s being mentioned in reviews and is a crowd pleaser.

You may have caught that there’s a truck in the entourage now. We’re carrying our own lights to make the show look and feel more dynamic. Our trailer was maxed out…full to overflowing. So we cut it loose and now put all the gear in a semi. It’s an easier and safer way to travel for the gear and for the crew. Lifting and stacking was taking a toll on everyone. Now we can get in and out of a venue more quickly with all cases on wheels.

We also spent a lot of time and effort in 2024 to clean up our social media accounts and give our website a facelift. If you check out any of those platforms, you’ll see we’re having a good time documenting our down time before and after a show. There’s a lot of joy in the air.

It’s an honor to have your valued support, and to be a part of Little River Band’s long history of great music and great shows. And it’s a lot of fun to let you see what we’re up to before the lights go down at showtime.

Thanks for staying in touch and keeping up with the tour. We’ll see you out there somewhere…

Take Care  
 LRB and Crew

# ABOUT LITTLE RIVER BAND

Little River Band was formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1975. It was originally a blend of musicians who had enjoyed success in other Australian acts. Their new focus was to get airplay on American radio, and they achieved that goal with good songwriting, powerful vocals, and guitar harmonies. They immediately claimed their place as one of the great vocal bands of the ‘70s and ‘80s.

Between 1976 and 1983, chart success in America included the following singles: It’s a Long Way There, Help Is on Its Way, Happy Anniversary, Reminiscing, Lady, Cool Change, Lonesome Loser, The Night Owls, Take It Easy On Me, Man On Your Mind, We Two, and The Other Guy.  
Worldwide album and CD sales now top 30 million. LRB also set a Billboard record in 1982 for having Top 10 US hits for 6 consecutive years…the first band ever to achieve that mark. According to BMI, Reminiscing has garnered rare status with over 5 million airplays on America radio…and Lady is close behind with over 4 million airplays. LRB was rightfully inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) Hall of Fame at the 18th Annual ARIA Music Awards of 2004. In 2015 the band received the award for Musical Entertainer of the Year from the G2E group…an international panel of judges that ranks casino entertainment.

**2025 brings LRB to it’s 50th Anniversary**. The calendar is filling up fast, with 75 shows booked…including a trip to New Zealand where, per capita, the band has sold more albums and CDs than any other territory. **The Happy Anniversary Tour** will go coast to coast in the US and Canada from Jan to Dec.

Current band membership is anchored by bassist and lead singer Wayne Nelson…a 45-year LRB veteran. He is joined on stage by keyboardist and Dove Award winning producer Chris Marion, drummer Ryan Ricks, and guitarists Colin Whinnery and Bruce Wallace. These great musicians have writing, touring, and recording credits that include legendary artists like Jim Messina, Kenny Loggins, Glenn Frey, Christopher Cross, Warren Zevon, America, Lonestar, Loretta Lynn, Wynona Judd, Sir George Martin, David Gates, Garth Brooks, Oak Ridge Boys, Steven Curtis Chapman, Randy Houser, Joe Diffie, Kim Carnes, Shane McAnally, Dierks Bentley, Trace Adkins, Montgomery Gentry, and Gretchen Wilson. All five are accomplished singers and deliver the signature LRB lead vocals and harmonies at every show.

This lineup brings fresh energy and arrangements to the classic hits, making new memories for the audience out of each live performance. It’s always fun to watch as people are swept up by the show’s vitality and the volume of hits from LRB’s history. You’ll see plenty of people mouthing the words…”I love this song…I forgot it was one of Little River Band’s hits!” When you pair that with dynamic new songs being created by the band, audiences feel the power of an act with a rich history and a fantastic corps of songwriters making new music.

Eagles founding member, the late Glenn Frey, joined with LRB as a guest artist in 1988 for 2 Australian tours…culminating with a live TV performance at Expo ’88. He spoke from the heart at that last show when he dubbed Little River Band “the best singing band in the world” in front of 125,000 concert goers. # ABOUT LITTLE RIVER BAND

Little River Band was formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1975. It was originally a blend of musicians who had enjoyed success in other Australian acts. Their new focus was to get airplay on American radio, and they achieved that goal with good songwriting, powerful vocals, and guitar harmonies. They immediately claimed their place as one of the great vocal bands of the ‘70s and ‘80s.

Between 1976 and 1983, chart success in America included the following singles: It’s a Long Way There, Help Is on Its Way, Happy Anniversary, Reminiscing, Lady, Cool Change, Lonesome Loser, The Night Owls, Take It Easy On Me, Man On Your Mind, We Two, and The Other Guy.  
Worldwide album and CD sales now top 30 million. LRB also set a Billboard record in 1982 for having Top 10 US hits for 6 consecutive years…the first band ever to achieve that mark. According to BMI, Reminiscing has garnered rare status with over 5 million airplays on America radio…and Lady is close behind with over 4 million airplays. LRB was rightfully inducted into the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) Hall of Fame at the 18th Annual ARIA Music Awards of 2004. In 2015 the band received the award for Musical Entertainer of the Year from the G2E group…an international panel of judges that ranks casino entertainment.

**2025 brings LRB to it’s 50th Anniversary**. The calendar is filling up fast, with 75 shows booked…including a trip to New Zealand where, per capita, the band has sold more albums and CDs than any other territory. **The Happy Anniversary Tour** will go coast to coast in the US and Canada from Jan to Dec.

Current band membership is anchored by bassist and lead singer Wayne Nelson…a 45-year LRB veteran. He is joined on stage by keyboardist and Dove Award winning producer Chris Marion, drummer Ryan Ricks, and guitarists Colin Whinnery and Bruce Wallace. These great musicians have writing, touring, and recording credits that include legendary artists like Jim Messina, Kenny Loggins, Glenn Frey, Christopher Cross, Warren Zevon, America, Lonestar, Loretta Lynn, Wynona Judd, Sir George Martin, David Gates, Garth Brooks, Oak Ridge Boys, Steven Curtis Chapman, Randy Houser, Joe Diffie, Kim Carnes, Shane McAnally, Dierks Bentley, Trace Adkins, Montgomery Gentry, and Gretchen Wilson. All five are accomplished singers and deliver the signature LRB lead vocals and harmonies at every show.

This lineup brings fresh energy and arrangements to the classic hits, making new memories for the audience out of each live performance. It’s always fun to watch as people are swept up by the show’s vitality and the volume of hits from LRB’s history. You’ll see plenty of people mouthing the words…”I love this song…I forgot it was one of Little River Band’s hits!” When you pair that with dynamic new songs being created by the band, audiences feel the power of an act with a rich history and a fantastic corps of songwriters making new music.

Eagles founding member, the late Glenn Frey, joined with LRB as a guest artist in 1988 for 2 Australian tours…culminating with a live TV performance at Expo ’88. He spoke from the heart at that last show when he dubbed Little River Band “the best singing band in the world” in front of 125,000 concert goers. The current lineup of LRB takes that accolade to heart each and every time they perform.

![Image 20: WN 114](https://reallittleriverband.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/WN-114.jpg)

### Wayne Nelson

Bass

After a Chicago band named Koala (!) split up, Wayne moved to LA in 1978 where he joined Jim Messina’s band. Messina and Little River Band toured together in ’79. LRB asked Nelson to join for their next tour of Australia, Europe, and America. 41 years later, Nelson has seen many musicians and singers come in and out of the LRB family. His view on all those lineup changes…”In all these years with LRB, I’ve sung, played, and rearranged our music with many different lineups, each with a different interpretation and style. This group of guys is unique in that we all cut our teeth on the same types of music when we were young. We have the utmost respect for the history of the band, and for what Little River Band songs mean to our fans…but we always look for a way to bring something new to the stage. We have fun exploring new ways to deliver the songs – recognizable and powerful, with new twists that will delight those fans who like to listen deep and analyze…

![Image 21: CM 106](https://reallittleriverband.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/CM-106.jpg)

### Chris Marion

Keys

After college, Chris moved to Nashville and began his playing career, garnering nominations for 4 Dove awards from the Gospel Music Assoc. In 1992, he joined with partner Danny Myrick to form Western Flyer and later worked with artists such as Garth Brooks and The Oak Ridge Boys. In early 2005, he entered the Little River Band family, and has recorded 5 CDs with the band since then.

And college did well by Chris. He has taken his music education on stage with spectacular orchestral arrangements for LRB’s music. 2019 will bring that music to the world with the release of a new LRB Orchestral CD…title to be determined!

![Image 22: RR 3](https://reallittleriverband.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/RR-3.jpg)

### Ryan Ricks

Drums

After graduating from Belmont College in Nashville TN, Ryan played and sang with Lacy J Dalton for a few years. He went on to tour in his own band and ended up putting down the drumsticks and singing background vocals for Loretta Lynn. He married his wife Terri, adopted a beautiful little girl from China, changed careers into the computer software world and left music for about 15 years. Only after a call from an old friend, Rich Herring, did he get back to playing drums and singing with Little River Band. He’s loving it.

![Image 23: CW 105](https://reallittleriverband.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/CW-105.jpg)

### Colin Whinnery

Lead Guitar

Colin Whinnery is an accomplished Nashville musician, songwriter, and engineer. He has toured as a guitar player with Wynonna Judd, Lonestar, Bryan White, and Savannah Jack, On bass, he’s worked with Carolyn Dawn Johnson, Billy Gilman, Bryan White, and Tim Rushlow from Little Texas.

Colin’s songwriting credits include cuts for Triple Scoop Music Licensing, and have been placed in multiple TV shows…The Young and The Restless, All About Us, Huff, One Life to Live, and All My Children. In stark contrast, he has engineered sessions for Willie Nelson and Jamie O’Hara, to name just a few.

He brings this wide range of experience to the stage with Little River  
 Band, adding a fresh energy to the rhythm section, and to the vocal stack.  
 And he’s already making his mark as a lead singer as well.

![Image 24: BW 107](https://reallittleriverband.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/BW-107-scaled.jpg)

### Bruce Wallace

Guitar

Nashville Singer-Songwriter and Guitarist Bruce Wallace plays rhythm guitar and adds a new layer to the vocal harmonies. The addition of Bruce to the line-up has added to the energy of the already highly energized LRB.

Bruce is an Oklahoma native with an accomplished career as a musician and songwriter. He has performed with superstars such as Wynonna, Kid Rock, Shelby Lynne, Mindy Smith, and David Gates (of Bread).

He has also written with hit songwriters Liz Rose, Randy Bachman, Rachel Proctor, Dave Berg, and Victoria Banks to name a few. Most recently his music can be heard on releases by Trace Adkins (“Damn You Bubba”), Dierks Bentley (“Gonna Die Young”), Montgomery Gentry (“So Called Life”), and Katie Armiger.

Keyboardist Chris Marion is a Dove Award winning producer. Chris is the creator of all the orchestral arrangements and charts on The Big Box. It is amazing to watch him play, sing, and conduct from his riser!

Nashville Singer-Songwriter and Guitarist Bruce Wallace plays rhythm guitar and adds a new layer to the vocal harmonies. The addition of Bruce to the line-up has added to the energy of the already highly energized LRB.

Drummer Ryan Ricks has locked down the rhythm section, and rounds out the vocals with his incredible range. Great singing drummers are rare…and LRB is lucky to have Ryan as part of that all-important vocal blend.

Nashville Guitarist Colin Whinnery plays rhythm and lead guitar, and shares lead vocal duties with Wayne. He brings a brand new voice and a fresh outlook to the rhythm section.

Early 2014 saw the release of Little River Band’s,**‘**Cuts Like a Diamond,’on Frontiers Records. “What If You’re Wrong,” went to #1 and stayed there for 3 weeks says Jim Shoe of CLASSX Radio.“Forever You, Forever Me,”and“You Dream, I’ll Drive,”both climbed into the station’s TOP 3.

In November of 2016, LRB released,**‘**The Hits…Revisited,’ on Wurld Records – a CD consisting of 9 re-recorded hits along with 2 new songs, written by Wayne, Chris, and Rich.  Kris Kristofferson attended one of their concerts in California. He came backstage after the concert and he told LRB that their harmonies are “better than the Beatles.”

May of 2017 brought the release of ‘The Big Box’ – a box set consisting of 6 disc’s and featuring a DVD with live footage from their 40 th Anniversary Tour.

In 2020, lead singer and bass player Wayne Nelson celebrated a personal and professional milestone of being a member of Little River Band for 40 years. That makes Wayne Nelson the longest standing member in the history of LRB. In partnership with Time Life, the band released a “Live” orchestral accompanied CD of the hits called “Black Tie.” This masterpiece of audio golden nuggets continues to thrill and sooth today.

In 2021, the CD Fan Favorites was released to the fans after they voted on their favorite songs from albums released since the year 2000. This album is a fan exclusive and continues to receive rave reviews from the beloved “Night Owls.”

Bringing their vocal and musical energy along with great arrangements to their timeless classic hits, each show creates new memories for the audience. The band enjoys watching their fans fall in love with the songs all over again as they are swept up by the show’s powerful performance and the volume of hits from _LRB_’s history.

With over 100 dates scheduled or being scheduled for their 2021-22 tour, Little River Band is hotter than ever – selling out shows and making music from coast to coast – continuing their legacy of being **“the****best singing band in the world.”**
